title: setqca: Native Python Crisp-Set and Fuzzy-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis
description: setqca is an open-source Python library implementing the mathematical core of Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA) natively, without wrapping the R QCA package. It provides crisp, three-anchor direct fuzzy and explicit indirect calibration with diagnostics; a typed configurational expression system with a structural parser; set-theoretic parameters of fit for sufficiency and necessity including PRI, RoN and unique coverage; systematic necessity screening that separates genuine findings from trivial necessity; case-level sufficiency diagnostics; complete truth tables that record why each row was excluded; exact classical Quine-McCluskey minimisation with an inspectable prime-implicant chart; conservative, parsimonious and intermediate solutions following Ragin and Sonnett; multi-value QCA minimised as multi-value cubes rather than Boolean indicators; and robustness sweeps over calibration anchors and truth-table thresholds. Every component is verified against the reference R QCA implementation on canonical datasets, with the two known divergences characterised and pinned by tests.
